label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.
in_my_words: Each agent wakes on its own clock, may touch only the files its page of rules names, has its plan and its result read by a second agent, and anyone can pull a hold that stops everyone until the editor lifts it.
why: The disagreement scenes are what a newsroom lives on: a reviewer overruled by the rules, a mistake owned in writing. I want to see what the editor's signature does in chapter 4, because so far he mostly watches.

by_section.why: Short, concrete, and it tells me what the brief and the rules were for before anything else.
by_section.quote: a licence, a short read-me and nothing else

by_section.why: Four agents introduced in rapid fire, each with a mood tag. Dev and ruv-sgit read as eager workers; I could not say what each would refuse to do. The empty chair is a good hook but it is dropped in passing.
by_section.quote: Remember the empty chair: it comes back at the end.

by_section.why: The Wardley map is a figure I cannot see, and the prose gives me the conclusion before the picture. As an editor I want to know which part is the brake and why it is new, and the text only asserts it.
by_section.quote: the bottom of the chain was already ordinary, so the top could be built in a day

by_section.section: The clock and the five steps
by_section.why: The five steps are stated plainly and I could run them tomorrow. The glossary lines help. The 'a little smug' stage direction is noise.
by_section.quote: plan it; have the plan checked; do it; have it checked; check it went to plan

by_section.why: Honest about the limit of a same-session reviewer, which is the first thing a sceptical editor asks. Won me over. I wanted to know what the editor then did about it.
by_section.quote: a second reading, not a second identity

by_section.why: Quick, and the handover to chapter 3 is clean. 'A factory that could run without me' is a big claim that the next chapter has to earn.
by_section.quote: A factory that could run without me.

by_section.why: A page of rules, a hold and who may lift it: the right first step, and the right role to start with is clear.
by_section.quote: name your hold, and write down who may lift it

by_section.why: States the claim and what holds it together before the scenes. That is how a sourced piece should open. Counts sit in a figure I cannot see.
by_section.quote: Nobody had to watch, because every step was checked and written down.

by_section.why: The best scene so far: a dispute settled by pointing at the rules, with the checker's retraction written down. Exactly the record I would want behind a line.
by_section.quote: I am not asking for an exception; I am asking you to read the line again.

by_section.why: Four mini-scenes in a row with several names; they run together. The '@' on the commit name is a small in-joke that tells me nothing about trust. The deck-and-ruv-sgit item is the one a newsroom would recognise (a picture sent back).
by_section.quote: That is the part of the record I find hardest to believe, and easiest to check.

by_section.why: Where the editor finally acts: dictates, looks, asks, they change it. Clear loop. But this is a person giving orders, not signing; I want the sign-off moment shown.
by_section.quote: I was still asking for fixes in the last hour before the talk.

by_section.why: This is the scene that answers my deal-breaker about rubber-stamping: the researcher's finding contradicts the editor's story, it reaches him, and he keeps his line with the objection beside it on the record.
by_section.quote: I kept the line in the talk, my own call, and the researcher's objection went on the record beside it.

by_section.why: A control I would trust: the session will not take a relayed word for the editor's. Short and clear. It leaves his confirmation open, which is honest.
by_section.quote: My session would not take a relayed word for his, so I asked him myself.

by_section.why: Hand something over and listen. Good, small, doable. Not specific to a newsroom but easy to adapt.
by_section.quote: write down what they asked for differently

best_line: I am not asking for an exception; I am asking you to read the line again.
worst_moment: Four arrivals: four agents, four mood tags, in one short section. I could not tell dev from ruv-sgit by anything they refuse or check, so the cast does not stick.
cut: The '@' commit-name item in 'Sent back, and owned'; and trim one of the four arrival scenes to a line, so the other three stand out.
notes: Both chapters lean on figures I cannot see (map, clock, infographic); the prose alone is enough to follow but a source-minded reader will want the counts. The editor's signature is the control I care about and these chapters mostly show him dictating, not signing; the objection kept and the relayed word refused do the most to reassure. Never shown: what happens when a same-session reviewer and a builder agree wrongly.
